tagline: Take a finding to a fix — one gated, logged command at a time.
lore: Amarok, the giant wolf of Inuit legend that hunts alone in the night — here he carries the operator's order to a Linux host over SSH: check it, fix it, prove it.
problem: The pack can tell you what is wrong; fixing it still means logging into hosts one by one, guessing why a scan credential failed, and patching from a plugin's solution text by hand. That work is slow, error-prone, and rarely logged.
does: Amarok checks Linux hosts read-only — health, login, "does this path exist?" and a strict pre-flight — and turns Tenable's own solution text into a remediation plan you review, then deploys it to one canary host and, after a separate click, rolls it out to the rest. Every button acts on one Target set and shows what will happen before you confirm. Every command on every host lands in a hash-chained log.

glance.caption: Amarok's At a glance: commands run (today, 7 days, hosts touched), problems in the last 7 days (failures, auth failures, host keys changed now, commands on hosts not in navi.db) and remediation readiness (plans not yet deployed, Linux hosts, runs in progress, hash chain check).

capabilities: every action uses the same host list shown in a bar at the top; a preview built from the exact request lists the hosts, the policy and the undo story.

one-confirm pre-flight with strict host keys — login, sudo, live OS group, package-manager lock and holds, installed → candidate vs fixed for every package, reboot state and whether a downgrade is still possible — plus health checks with a health verdict, login test and path check.

the plugin's solution and output (rpm and dpkg package pairs, kernels, upstream versions) become one plan per OS group — every affected package in one transaction — checked by a deterministic allow-list validator.
two confirmed clicks: one non-crown canary first; roll out unlocks only when the canary reads Fixed. Crown jewels always run last.

Fixed only when every package reaches its distro fixed build; otherwise Upgraded (fix not proven or still vulnerable), No change, Already fixed, Not installed, Held, Package manager busy, Step failed or Unknown state — with reboot and service-restart flags.
free-form commands and file copies on the Target set, with a typed host count for any multi-host run and an abort switch.
how: Amarok drives `navi action push` (SSH to one Linux host per call) and reads plans from your local navi.db. Every remote action needs writes enabled, remote execution separately enabled (NAVI_REMOTE_CODE_EXECUTION) and a confirm; the server re-checks the confirmed host count. Tabs: Overview, Inspect, Remediate, Command & files, Activity.
who: Linux and infrastructure teams who remediate, scan engineers chasing credential failures, and VM leads who want fixes that are reviewed, staged and logged.
better: Argos and the explorers hand a finding to Amarok as a proposal — never merged, never auto-run. Chronos shows which hosts failed credentials; Amarok tells you why. After a fix, Sync navi.db pulls the new scan state so Sköll and Nemesis can count it.
different: plans start from Tenable's own solution text, not a model's guess.
A validator, not a second model
an allow-list and deny-list decide what can deploy; a model talked into `curl | sh` still can't ship it.
every command on every host lands in a tamper-evident log.
cta: Send Amarok after the finding — reviewed, staged, logged.
